doc.title: Stefon Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2020

title: Improvisation versus composition
summary: Harris calls composition very slow improvisation, discovered rather than owned, tied to a logic underlying all being.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Yes. And as you notably said in your TED talk, when you play an F sharp over an F chord you better know how to work with that. Okay Michelle.

One more question and this might be the last one that has come in, it says can you speak to the relationship between improvisation and composition? What about the cultural politics of that distinction?

I mean I honestly think of composition as just really really slow improvisation. It’s the same idea. It’s just that when you’re improvising it’s happening quickly. But fundamentally I don’t see it as the idea that I own the music, that I’m so special, that I’m creating something. I will literally go [scats] and go no that’s not it, I don’t know why that’s not it. Then go [scats] oh that’s it. In my mind the reason that I know that that’s the right note is that it already exists. There are these beautiful — I also love physics, love science and I find that there are, in theory there is this beautiful logic that governs the behavior of all being, whether from plants — there’s some logic that holds everything together. And what’s happening to me is the more I study the more I bring to mind, I’m able to see those natural connections that exist. Not that I’m creating them. But the more perceptive I become the easier it is to capture the music that’s there.
